chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated from Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), regarding:

A man deposited two dinars with another man, and that man deposited one dinar with him. One dinar was lost from them. He (the Imam) said: 'He gives the owner of the two dinars one dinar, and they share the remaining dinar between them in two halves.'

key_terms.صَاحِبَ الدِّينَارَيْنِ: the owner of the two dinars

ai.seo_question: How is a lost deposit divided when two people have mutually deposited different amounts with each other?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the principle of proportional compensation in mixed deposits, ensuring fairness when specific items are indistinguishable. It reflects the Shia juristic approach to *qismah* (division) in cases of mutual trust (*istiwda'*), prioritizing equitable distribution over strict individual liability. The hadith is recorded in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, a primary source for Ja'fari fiqh, highlighting the practical application of justice in commercial transactions.
